entry.title: Re: NVIDIA 590 driver drops Pascal and lower support / switch to -open
entry.content:
Heads-up - the 'nvidia-580xx-dkms' from the AUR currently doesn't work with the LTS 6.12.66-1 (and older) kernel - there is a note on https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/nvidia-580xx-utils about this from a few days back.  I just found this out the hard way.

Rather than roll back, I decided the easiest way forward was to install 6.18.6-arch1-1 alongside the LTS and run a grub-mkconfig to make it available as a fall-back until this gets fixed, and all is now well, but be aware of this if you're running an LTS kernel.

entry.title: Re: NVIDIA 590 driver drops Pascal and lower support / switch to -open
entry.content:
VectorSpiral wrote:

So are the normal nvidia packages no longer going to be available from this point forward?

announcement wrote:

GTX 10xx series and older cards must switch to the legacy proprietary branch to maintain support:

  • Uninstall the official 'nvidia', 'nvidia-lts', or 'nvidia-dkms' packages.

  • Install 'nvidia-580xx-dkms' from the AUR

You can still switch to the AUR packages if you have >10xx series card, but it's not supported by Arch.

entry.title: Re: NVIDIA 590 driver drops Pascal and lower support / switch to -open
entry.content:
So are the normal nvidia packages no longer going to be available from this point forward? I've had problems with the nvidia-open branch beforehand that were not present in the non-open equivalent.

I have to admit that I'm also a little confused by the announcement as it seems like switching the proprietary packages to the -open ones and Nvidia's support depreciation are two separate things, as people with the older cards are still unsupported on the -open branch and have to stay on the (legacy) proprietary branch anyways.

entry.title: Re: NVIDIA 590 driver drops Pascal and lower support / switch to -open
entry.content:
gromit wrote:
Peter Jung via arch-announce wrote:

With the update to driver version 590, the NVIDIA driver no longer supports Pascal (GTX 10xx) GPUs or older. We will replace the 'nvidia' package with 'nvidia-open', 'nvidia-dkms' with 'nvidia-open-dkms', and 'nvidia-lts' with 'nvidia-lts-open'.

(...)

Users with Turing (20xx and GTX 1650 series) and newer GPUs will automatically transition to the open kernel modules on upgrade and require no manual intervention.

Absolutely seamless migration from nvidia to nvidia-open. It's been years, but I came from a distro where switching drivers always gave me cold sweats because, more often than not, something went wrong. Well done to the entire team

Intervention required for Pascal/older users: Users with GTX 10xx series and older cards must switch to the legacy proprietary branch to maintain support:

  • Uninstall the official 'nvidia', 'nvidia-lts', or 'nvidia-dkms' packages.

  • Install 'nvidia-580xx-dkms' from the AUR

(...)

https://archlinux.org/news/nvidia-590-d … l-modules/

I was missing `linux-headers` too (didn't think about it first after years without using DKMS).
Thanks you raggerv8 for making my brain switch on ;-)
Most Arch users will do it logically: switching from the nvidia default arch package to AUR requires to have `linux-headers` installed before installing 'nvidia-580xx-dkms' (as for any DKMS package).

  • Install 'nvidia-580xx-dkms' from the AUR

Users with Turing (20xx and GTX 1650 series) and newer GPUs will automatically transition to the open kernel modules on upgrade and require no manual intervention.

https://archlinux.org/news/nvidia-590-d … l-modules/

There is a typo in the post, nvidia-lts-open VS nvidia-open-lts

entry.title: NVIDIA 590 driver drops Pascal and lower support / switch to -open
entry.content:
Peter Jung via arch-announce wrote:

With the update to driver version 590, the NVIDIA driver no longer supports Pascal (GTX 10xx) GPUs or older. We will replace the 'nvidia' package with 'nvidia-open', 'nvidia-dkms' with 'nvidia-open-dkms', and 'nvidia-lts' with 'nvidia-lts-open'.

Impact: Updating the NVIDIA packages on systems with Pascal, Maxwell, or older cards will fail to load the driver, which may result in a broken graphical environment.

Intervention required for Pascal/older users: Users with GTX 10xx series and older cards must switch to the legacy proprietary branch to maintain support:

  • Uninstall the official 'nvidia', 'nvidia-lts', or 'nvidia-dkms' packages.

  • Install 'nvidia-580xx-dkms' from the AUR

Users with Turing (20xx and GTX 1650 series) and newer GPUs will automatically transition to the open kernel modules on upgrade and require no manual intervention.

https://archlinux.org/news/nvidia-590-d … l-modules/
